key_insight: A hybrid cross-modal attention model combining mammograms with clinical data improved early breast cancer detection in low-resource settings.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support more accurate, faster triage where radiology expertise and high-quality imaging are limited.
method: Used transformer-based cross-modal attention to fuse mammogram images with structured clinical variables.
Trained and validated on 2,560 mammograms from 1,024 patients across four Ethiopian referral hospitals.
Compared performance against image-only baselines and analyzed attention patterns for clinically ambiguous cases.
evidence_signal: The model achieved 97.8% accuracy, 97.2% sensitivity, 98.3% specificity, and an AUC of 0.987, with only 3.2% degradation on low-quality images.
watch_item: Generalizability beyond the Ethiopian hospital dataset and real-world workflow integration still need external validation.
paper_title: Hybrid Cross-Modal Attention Network for Early Breast Cancer Detection in Low-Resource Clinical Settings
